text:
sophie: ACME support ping — customers seeing intermittent 502/504s against HostedAPI during large streaming embed jobs (high concurrency).
sophie: repro window: ~2026-01-18 15:10-15:20 UTC, multiple tenants affected but ACME hit hardest. sample req_id=acme-req-9f3a
sophie: quick curl repro we ran: curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'Tenant-ID: acme' -d @big.json https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
maria: received 3 different trace ids from ACME, pasted below — they match the same gateway egress timestamp
sophie: attached logs from customer (redacted) show upstream response timeout then 502 from frontdoor
elena: can you paste the gateway/edge logs and an envoy admin snapshot? also need which region (eu1/us1)
tim: eu1 — grabbing envoy logs now. quick grep showed repeated "upstream reset before response completed" followed by "HTTP/2 stream closed"
ops-bot: alert: frontdoor-eu1: increased 5xx rate (502/504) 15:12 UTC — rolling window spike 4x baseline
elena: hypothesis: idle/keepalive window exhaustion + midproxy preemption. when upstreams delay for >120ms we see L7 router preempt streams to keep headroom.
raj: we recently rolled a change to L7Router: "preempt_on_queue_bump=true" to avoid head-of-line for tenant fairness. could be triggering early resets when auth backend sleeps
sophie: ACME says it started after a customer-side billing sync at ~15:08 which added bursts of token-refresh calls
tim: envoy extract (eu1 frontdoor) snippet:
"[2026-01-18T15:12:03.123Z] upstream/0: remote reset, peer closed connection, code=INTERNAL_RESET"
"[2026-01-18T15:12:03.124Z] router: upstream response timeout, status=0"
"[2026-01-18T15:12:03.125Z] connection: stream reset by application, error=STREAM_CANCEL"
elena: can you run a repro with an explicit --no-keepalive client header and one with http2 keepalive to compare? also need nginx midproxy config (if any)
maria: ACME gave a sample flow: long-lived stream to embeddings endpoint with intermittent auth-refresh calls over same TCP.
sophie: steps we used to repro:
1) spawn 40 concurrent streaming embedding requests (chunked) from the same tenant
2) every 10s trigger a short auth-refresh call that touches billing (simulates customer daemon)
3) after ~2m we see 10-15% requests get 502/504
tim: quick mitigation we tested in eu1: bump l7router.max_inflight_per_tenant from 8 -> 16 and increase upstream_idle_timeout 90s -> 180s. 5xxs dropped ~70% in canary
raj: longer-term fix options:
- revert preempt_on_queue_bump until we can do per-tenant backpressure
- move token-refresh calls to a separate connection pool (avoid head-of-line on same TCP)
- make L7Router preemption less aggressive for streaming endpoints
elena: for triage we need:
- full envoy access logs for the 15:10-15:25 window (include x-request-id)
- l7router stats: inflight_per_tenant, preempt_count, queue_depth
- customer request sample + response bytes
sophie: requested logs/trace from ACME (they sent three x-request-id values). asking for full logs now.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled l7router config to eu1 at 2026-01-18T14:40:12Z (change set cs-2781)
maria: ACME accepted the temporary workaround (reduce concurrency client-side) while we investigate :+1:
tim: quick reproducer for dev (use within cluster):
kubectl exec -it loadgen -- /bin/sh -c "seq 1 40 | xargs -n1 -P40 sh -c '\n  curl -s -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Tenant-ID: acme\" -d @big.json https://eu1-hosted.redwood/v1/embeddings &\n'"
elena: grep lines to pull from envoy logs:

kubectl logs envoy-xxxxx -n frontdoor --since=30m | egrep 'upstream reset|stream reset|router: upstream response timeout' > /tmp/edge-502s.log

sophie: next steps: collect requested logs, try the canary bump to l7router params in another region if safe, and confirm ACME behaviour after client concurrency reduction.
raj: I'll open a rollback PR for preempt_on_queue_bump in case canary shows regression.
maria: thanks team, keeping ACME updated. will post when we have more traces.
elena: noting action owners: tim (collect envoy logs + run canary bump), raj (prepare rollback PR), sophie/maria (customer comms). elena: ping me when logs uploaded :wave:
